newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ALFONZO HOMER RALLIES METS PAST PIRATES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ALFONZO HOMER RALLIES METS PAST PIRATES.

text.p: Edgardo Alfonzo's two-run homer with two out in the bottom of the eighth inning rallied the New York Mets to their third straight one-run win, 3-2 over the Pittsburgh Pirates Saturday.

Trailing 2-1, Mets pinch-hitter Jason Hardtke singled and stole second as John Olerud struck out. Alfonzo then hit a 1-0 pitch from Marc Wilkins (5-1) just over the wall in left-centre to make it 3-2.

"I'm not really a home run hitter," Alfonzo said. "But I can hit the ball out. At that point I was just trying to hit the ball hard. I saw it keep carrying and when it went out it was unbelievable. It felt great and I was really excited."

Alfonzo's homer stood as the game-winner after the Mets executed an exciting relay play in the ninth. With pinch-runner Kevin Polcovich on first, Jose Guillen doubled into the left-field corner but Butch Huskey cut the ball off.
He threw over Alfonzo, the primary relay man. But second baseman Carlos Baerga got it and fired a one-hopper to Todd Hundley, who one-handed it to nail Polcovich at the plate.
"It was a do-or-die type play," said Hundley. "On short hops you just put the glove down and hope its sticks there."
"I was ready," Baerga said. "Even though it was a short hop it was a good throw because if it's too high he's probably safe. It's really exciting."
"I was trying to hit Alfonzo, I don't know if he was too far out or I overthrew him," said Huskey. "But Carlos was where he was supposed to be and it turned out OK."
Mets starter Dave Mlicki (4-5) allowed two runs and six hits over eight innings, walking one and striking out seven. Greg McMichael worked the ninth and got his third save.
Pittsburgh has lost five straight and 10 of its last 12.
In San Diego, Eric Young and Andres Galarraga hit two-run homers and Larry Walker added a solo shot to power the Colorado Rockies to a 9-4 victory over the Padres.
Galarraga, who finished 4-for-5 with three singles, including his 21st homer, raised his league-leading RBI to 79. His 21 homers tie him with Walker and Houston's Jeff Bagwell for the league-lead.
Archie Cianfrocco hit a three-run homer for the Padres, who lost for the sixth time in seven games.
In Philadelphia, reserves Eduardo Perez, Andruw Jones and Tony Graffanino all homered as the Atlanta Braves handed the Phillies their season-high seventh straight loss, 9-8.
Jones played for Kenny Lofton (strained left groin). Perez started for Javier Lopez (bruised left knee). Graffanino started in place of Mark Lemke, who struck out as a pinch-hitter in the sixth.

Atlanta starter Denny Neagle had his worst outing of the season. He was knocked from the box after giving up six runs and 10 hits in 4 1/3 innings. In his previous three starts, Neagle had pitched 25 innings and thrown two shutouts.

In San Francisco, emergency starter Tom Candiotti allowed four hits over seven innings and Tripp Cromer had three hits and a career-high three RBI to lead the Los Angeles Dodgers to their fourth win in five games, an 11-0 rout of the Giants.
Making his first start of the season, Candiotti (4-2) walked one and struck out six in place of Ramon Martinez, who is suffering from a tender right shoulder.
San Francisco starter William VanLandingham (4-5) was reached for six runs and seven hits in five innings.
In Houston, Bagwell drove in two runs and Tim Bogar had a career-high three doubles to lead the Astros to their third win in four games, 7-3 over the Chicago Cubs.
Chris Holt (7-5) got the win, allowing three runs and five hits in 6 1/3 innings.
Cubs starter Frank Castillo (4-9) was reached for five runs and seven hits in 1 1/3 innings as the Cubs dropped their fourth straight.
In Montreal, Mike Lansing had an RBI double and scored in a three-run seventh inning and Vladimir Guerrero homered in his first game off the disabled list as the Expos edged the Florida Marlins 4-3.
Jeff Juden (8-2) allowed three runs over 7 2/3 innings as the Expos won for the 12th time in 14 games. Ugueth Urbina recorded the final four outs for his 13th save.
Guerrero, sidelined since June 5 with a pulled right hamstring, homered with one out in the fourth.
In St Louis, Todd Stottlemyre allowed two runs on eight hits over six innings as the Cardinals beat the Cincinnati Reds 6-2 to snap a five-game losing streak.
Royce Clayton's two-out, two-run single in the bottom of the third off Cincinnati starter Dave Burba (4-7) staked the Cardinals to a 4-0 lead.
Stottlemyre (5-5) won for the first time in four starts.
